glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
ananda-vihara.desc: Ananda Vihara, known locally as Ananda Rajar Prasad, is the biggest of the excavated monuments in the Mainamati complex at Kotbari. Like Shalban Vihara it was a square monastery with monks' cells around a central shrine, and next to it lies the largest ancient water tank in the area. Much of the site lies within or near the cantonment and is less tidy than Shalban, so it sees few visitors. Come with the museum's story in mind and the scale is impressive.
blocks: How to get there
From Kotbari or Cumilla town take a CNG or rickshaw; ask locals for 'Ananda Rajar Bari'.
Good to know
Parts of the Mainamati ridge are military land; follow signs and do not enter restricted areas.

glance: Khadi shops around Monohorpur and Kandirpar, Cumilla town
cumilla-khadi.desc: Khadi weaving in the Cumilla area grew strongly during the swadeshi and Gandhian movements, when hand-spun cloth was a protest against imported mill fabric. The cloth is coarse, breathable and comfortable in the heat. Today Cumilla's khadi shops sell kurtas, panjabis, saris and fabric by the metre, often in earthy colours, and the name 'Comillar khadi' is known across the country.

glance: Matri Bhandar and other old sweet shops around Monohorpur, Cumilla town
cumilla-roshmalai.desc: Roshmalai is made by poaching little discs of fresh chhana in syrup, then soaking them in milk that has been boiled down slowly until thick and creamy. Cumilla's version is known for its rich, slightly caramel milk and tender balls. Travellers on the highway stop to buy boxes to carry home, and the original shops near Monohorpur draw long queues.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
lalmai-chandi-temple.desc: Chandimura sits on the summit of the Lalmai hill in Barura upazila, south of Cumilla town. The main shrine is dedicated to the goddess Chandi (Kali), and a Shiva temple stands close by. A long stairway climbs the red-earth hill, and from the top you look across the flat fields of Cumilla. It draws pilgrims at festival times but few tourists on ordinary days.
blocks: How to get there
From Cumilla town take a CNG toward Lalmai/Barura and ask for Chandimura; the last stretch is on foot up the steps.
Good to know
Remove shoes at the temple. The steps are steep, so carry water and go early in hot weather.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
cumilla-jagannath-temple.desc: This temple is dedicated to Jagannath and is one of the oldest in the district; most accounts date it to 1761, though some local sources place it earlier. It was built as a 'seventeen-jewel' temple: eight small spires on the second level, eight on the third and one crowning the centre, which made it one of the tallest temples in the country. The images of Jagannath, Balaram and Subhadra here are said to have come from a temple in Tripura. Several spires are damaged now, but the terracotta brickwork is still worth a close look.
blocks: How to get there
Take a rickshaw or auto from Cumilla town; the temple is about 2 km to the south-east.
Good to know
Take off your shoes before going in and ask before photographing the images. Rath Yatra brings big crowds if you want to see the temple in festival mood.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
dharmasagar-dighi.desc: Dharmasagar is said to have been dug in the 15th century by Maharaja Dharma Manikya of Tripura to supply water during a famine. Today it is the town's favourite open space, with shady walkways, a park and paddle boats along its banks. Early mornings bring walkers and anglers, and evenings bring families and snack sellers.
blocks: How to get there
In central Cumilla town, a short rickshaw ride from Kandirpar.
Good to know
Go early morning or at sunset. Pick up roshmalai in nearby Monohorpur afterward.

bijoypur-pottery.desc: Bijoypur, in Cumilla Sadar Dakshin, is known for a long tradition of pottery run by the Rudrapal potter community, now organised as a cooperative. Artisans shape clay on wheels and by hand, fire it in kilns and paint pieces with simple designs. Visitors can see the process and buy household and decorative ware directly from the makers.
blocks: Good to know
Ask before entering workshops; buying directly supports the artisans.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
maynamati-war-cemetery.desc: This Commonwealth War Graves cemetery holds the graves of soldiers from Britain, India, Africa and elsewhere who died in this region during the Second World War, many of them in military hospitals nearby. Neat rows of headstones sit on a gentle slope among lawns and flowering trees. It is a quiet, reflective place, and a reminder that Cumilla was a major military base in the war.
blocks: How to get there
On the Cumilla–Sylhet road near Tipra Bazar, about 15 minutes by CNG from town.
Good to know
Keep noise low and do not walk on graves. Morning light is best for photos.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
mainamati-museum.desc: The Mainamati Museum stands beside Shalban Vihara at Kotbari and displays what archaeologists dug out of the Mainamati–Lalmai ruins. There are terracotta plaques showing people and animals, bronze Buddhas and Hindu deities, stone sculpture, coins and copper-plate inscriptions from the Deva and Chandra kingdoms of the 8th–12th centuries. Seeing the objects first makes the brick ruins outside far easier to understand. It is small enough to see in under an hour.
blocks: How to get there
From Cumilla town take a CNG or bus to Kotbari (about 30 minutes); the museum is beside the Shalban Vihara gate.
Good to know
Like most Archaeology Department sites it is usually closed on Sundays and has short hours on Mondays; check before you go.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
rupban-mura.desc: Rupban Mura is one of several smaller archaeological sites scattered across the Lalmai–Mainamati hills. It has excavated brick foundations of a Buddhist establishment on a low hilltop. Many visitors to Shalban Vihara skip it, so you may have the brickwork and the views over the ridge to yourself.
blocks: How to get there
Near Kotbari on the Cumilla–Kalirbazar road, a short ride from Shalban Vihara.
Good to know
Check whether the site is open on the day; ask the Shalban staff for directions.

glance: Markets along the Lalmai hills and roadside stalls near Kotbari
lalmai-jackfruit.desc: The red, well-drained soil of the Lalmai hills suits jackfruit trees, and every summer the ridges near Cumilla smell of ripening fruit. Farmers carry them to local markets and the highway, where they are sold by the piece. The sweet yellow pods are eaten fresh, and the seeds are roasted or cooked in curries.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
Ticketed (Department of Archaeology); foreigners pay more
shalban-vihara.desc: Shalban Vihara is the best-known of the Mainamati ruins in the Lalmai hills. It is a square monastery with rows of monks' cells around a central temple, built by kings of the Deva dynasty. Excavations here turned up coins, terracotta plaques and copper plates, many of which are shown in the Mainamati Museum next door. Walking the brick corridors in the late afternoon gives a real sense of a working monastic town.
blocks: How to get there
About 20–30 minutes by CNG from Cumilla town toward Kotbari.
Good to know
Museum and site usually close one day a week; check before going. Combine with the museum and Rupban Mura.

glance: 105 km to Cumilla by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
shah-shuja-mosque-cumilla.desc: The Shah Shuja Mosque stands in Mughaltuli in the old part of Cumilla town. Local tradition links it to the Mughal prince Shah Shuja, though no inscription has been found and its exact date is disputed. The prayer hall has three domes and corner towers in typical Mughal style, and later additions have been built around it. It is still in daily use and is a short rickshaw ride from Dharmasagar.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw to Mughaltuli in Cumilla town.
Good to know
Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly; women should check whether there is a separate area.
